title: armed-branch-push-watch races PR creation — every post-merge follow-up trips it
note: MEASURED 2026-09-21 on PR #12673, which is the follow-up to the reset's own merge. scripts/ci/check_armed_branch_push.py reported `dropped` (error, exit 1) on a HEALTHY push. Timing is the whole bug: #12668 squash-merged as 3ea2777 at 12:18 and GitHub deleted the branch; the branch was reset from the new main and A6 pushed at 12:25:43; #12673 was opened at 12:26:10. The watcher ran in that 27-second gap, when the branch's ONLY associated PR was the merged #12668 whose head.sha (1d596e2) is not the pushed sha (f3301d0). [!] THIS IS NOT A ONE-OFF. A PR cannot be opened for a branch that has not been pushed, so EVERY follow-up PR made the sanctioned way (git fetch origin main && git checkout -B <branch> origin/main) trips this between push and PR creation. The guard's premise -- that the PR it finds is the PR for this push -- is false during a branch reset. [!] DO NOT 'FIX' IT BY DOWNGRADING THE SEVERITY. The loss it exists for (#11846) is real, and a guard that cries wolf on the healthy path is how a guard gets ignored -- the desensitisation this repo already measured at 202 of 376 CRITICALs being one un-latched condition. Sharpen the condition. [!] THE DISCRIMINATOR, and it does NOT fall into the ancestry trap the script's own docstring warns about. That trap is asking whether a BRANCH commit reached main -- which a squash merge always answers no to. Ask the OPPOSITE: is the old PR's MERGE COMMIT an ancestor of the PUSHED commit? Branch correctly reset -> yes (3ea2777 is an ancestor of f3301d0), nothing lost, a new PR is coming. Genuine drop, i.e. more commits pushed onto the merged branch's old history -> no; the pre-merge head is the ancestor instead. A squash does not defeat that direction. [!] The script has an elaborate --self-test with a mutation-tested exact-sha comparison; extend it rather than loosening it, and add the branch-reset case as a NAMED fixture so the next person cannot re-introduce this by tightening something else. [!] DISPATCHED 2026-09-21, sonnet-5, fresh, ceiling $12 (this row carried no ceiling; one is set now). It earns its slot today because the manager's own pushes are the population it mis-grades: every follow-up PR made the sanctioned way trips it in the gap between push and PR creation. Lane told in terms to SHARPEN the condition and NOT downgrade the severity, and to CONSTRUCT both cases rather than implement the proposed discriminator on trust -- a reported hole beats a confident fix. [!] CLOSED 2026-09-21 AS ALREADY FIXED, AND THE LANE THAT ESTABLISHED IT WAS DISPATCHED IN ERROR BY THIS MANAGER. The fix landed in #12676 -- the SAME PR the handoff named as 'A7's pipeline + close-out contract + E10' -- and this row was never moved off `queued`. VERIFIED on main, not taken from the lane: scripts/ci/check_armed_branch_push.py defines RESET_FROM_MERGE, carries the merge-commit-ancestry discriminator, and has the branch-reset case as a named self-test fixture. Cost of the error: $0.93. [!] THE LESSON IS NOT 'READ MORE CAREFULLY', it is that a row's `state` was not moved by the PR that resolved it, so the register lied to the next reader in the direction of MORE work rather than less. Filed as PI-20260921-M06.
